unitPrice.description: Sell price per unit, THE monetary field on this endpoint. ServiceTitan silently IGNORES a field named `price` (it returns HTTP 200 and writes a $0.00 line), so unitPrice is the only way to set the amount. NEGATIVE values are allowed and are how an offsetting/credit line is expressed. REQUIRED when appending (no `id`): ST does NOT compute dynamic pricing on API-appended items, so an append without unitPrice lands at $0.00 and the tool rejects it. On an UPDATE (`id` present) you may omit it to leave the existing price alone, but that is UNPROBED: ST may bind the omitted field as null and zero the line. The tool warns at dryRun and the post-write verify-read reports amount_mismatch if the price moved.

skuName.description: Pricebook CODE of the item (e.g. "SKU1"), not its display name. REQUIRED: ServiceTitan resolves an adjustment line by SKU name. Unlike the invoice-items PATCH endpoint, `skuId` is silently IGNORED here. The code is checked against the live pricebook before the write (an exact code wins; case and hyphen variants such as "ab12" for "AB-12" are accepted when they match one row) and the matched row's exact code is what gets sent. A name that matches nothing, or more than one row, is rejected: an unresolvable name would be dropped by ServiceTitan and produce an empty $0.00 adjustment invoice that cannot be deleted via the API.

cost.description: Line cost basis (not the sell amount, see unitPrice)

unitPrice.description: Sell price per unit, THE monetary field on this endpoint. ServiceTitan silently IGNORES a field named `price` (HTTP 200, $0.00 line). NEGATIVE values are allowed and are how an offsetting adjustment line is expressed, e.g. unitPrice: -100 to back out revenue booked on the parent invoice. Omitting it creates the line at $0.00 (ServiceTitan does not apply dynamic pricing to API-created invoice lines), which is almost never what an adjustment wants, so the tool warns when it is omitted.
